question: Ve Wimbledonu musí tenisté hrát skoro celí v bílém. Pravidlo vzniklo už v 19. století. Co měla bílá barva skrýt?
source_excerpt: white was chosen to minimize their visibility, as sweat is more apparent on colorful clothing

extra.why_interesting: Czechs follow Wimbledon closely thanks to Navrátilová, Kvitová, Krejčíková and Vondroušová, and most assume the white rule is just snobbish tradition. Its real purpose is a very human one: hiding sweat. The answer can be worked out by thinking about what shows least on white cloth.
extra.verification_notes: Widely documented that the Victorian-era all-white rule was meant to hide sweat stains; no newer development changes this (https://www.si.com/tennis/wimbledon-notoriously-strict-dress-code-players-fascinating-origin).

explanation: Propocené skvrny na oblečení se ve viktoriánské Anglii považovaly za neslušné a na bílé látce jsou vidět nejméně. Proto i Kvitová a Vondroušová zvedaly wimbledonskou trofej v bílém.
